name: Castillo San Felipe del Morro

price.text: $10 · covers both forts for 24 hours · 15 and under free

description: The great sea fort at the tip of Old San Juan: six levels of walls, tunnels and garitas above the Atlantic, and a huge lawn where families fly kites.
tips: No booking: pay at the entrance by card or phone; the park doesn’t take cash.
One $10 pass covers San Cristóbal too, for 24 hours.
Check the day’s opening hours on nps.gov/saju; they have changed over the years. Also closed on Thanksgiving.
Go early: there’s little shade on the lawn or the upper levels.

audio.script: El Morro guards the narrow entrance to San Juan Bay. Spain began it in the fifteen thirties and kept building for more than two centuries, until it rose six levels above the sea. It held off Francis Drake in 1595 and a Dutch siege in 1625, though English troops took it briefly in 1598. Look for the garitas, the domed sentry boxes on the walls: they have become the symbol of Puerto Rico. The fort is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

scripts.es: El Morro vigila la estrecha entrada de la bahía de San Juan. España lo comenzó en la década de 1530 y siguió construyéndolo durante más de dos siglos, hasta que alcanzó seis niveles sobre el mar. Resistió a Francis Drake en 1595 y un asedio holandés en 1625, aunque tropas inglesas lo tomaron brevemente en 1598. Busca las garitas, las casetas de vigilancia con cúpula sobre las murallas: se han convertido en el símbolo de Puerto Rico. El fuerte forma parte de un sitio del Patrimonio Mundial de la UNESCO.
scripts.fr: El Morro garde l’étroite entrée de la baie de San Juan. L’Espagne l’a commencé dans les années 1530 et a continué à le bâtir pendant plus de deux siècles, jusqu’à six niveaux au-dessus de la mer. Il a repoussé Francis Drake en 1595 et un siège hollandais en 1625, même si des troupes anglaises l’ont pris brièvement en 1598. Cherchez les garitas, les guérites à coupole sur les remparts : elles sont devenues le symbole de Porto Rico. Le fort fait partie d’un site du patrimoine mondial de l’UNESCO.
scripts.pt: El Morro guarda a estreita entrada da baía de San Juan. A Espanha começou a construí-lo nos anos 1530 e continuou por mais de dois séculos, até ele chegar a seis níveis acima do mar. Resistiu a Francis Drake em 1595 e a um cerco holandês em 1625, embora tropas inglesas o tenham tomado por pouco tempo em 1598. Procure as garitas, as guaritas com cúpula nas muralhas: elas viraram o símbolo de Porto Rico. O forte faz parte de um Patrimônio Mundial da UNESCO.
scripts.de: El Morro bewacht die schmale Einfahrt in die Bucht von San Juan. Spanien begann den Bau in den 1530er-Jahren und baute mehr als zwei Jahrhunderte weiter, bis die Festung sechs Ebenen über dem Meer aufragte. Sie hielt Francis Drake 1595 und einer niederländischen Belagerung 1625 stand, auch wenn englische Truppen sie 1598 kurz einnahmen. Achten Sie auf die Garitas, die Wachhäuschen mit Kuppel auf den Mauern: Sie sind zum Symbol Puerto Ricos geworden. Die Festung gehört zu einer UNESCO-Welterbestätte.
scripts.it: El Morro sorveglia lo stretto ingresso della baia di San Juan. La Spagna iniziò a costruirlo negli anni Trenta del Cinquecento e continuò per più di due secoli, fino a sei livelli sopra il mare. Resistette a Francis Drake nel 1595 e a un assedio olandese nel 1625, anche se truppe inglesi lo presero per breve tempo nel 1598. Cercate le garitas, le garitte con la cupola sulle mura: sono diventate il simbolo di Porto Rico. Il forte fa parte di un sito Patrimonio dell’Umanità UNESCO.

closed_source.text: National Park Service, San Juan National Historic Site

access.note: A walk across the open lawn to reach it, then steep ramps and stairs inside. Bring water and hats, and plan rests; benches are few.

ride: Ask to be dropped as close to the entrance as allowed; the last stretch is on foot across the lawn.

name: Castillo San Cristóbal

price.text: $10 · covers both forts for 24 hours · 15 and under free

description: The biggest fort Spain built in the Americas, guarding the city from the land side, with sweeping views and the legendary Garita del Diablo.
tips: Same $10 pass as El Morro, valid 24 hours. Card or phone only.
Closer to the taxis and buses at the east end of Old San Juan than El Morro.
Also closed on Thanksgiving.

audio.script: San Cristóbal faced the other way from El Morro: it protected San Juan from an attack by land. Finished in the late seventeen hundreds, it is the largest fortification Spain built in the Americas, with layer upon layer of walls, so that taking one would leave an attacker exposed to the next. At the far end stands the Garita del Diablo, the devil’s sentry box, where legend says guards on night watch simply vanished.

scripts.es: San Cristóbal miraba en dirección contraria a El Morro: protegía San Juan de un ataque por tierra. Terminado a finales del siglo dieciocho, es la mayor fortificación que España construyó en las Américas, con murallas superpuestas para que, si un atacante tomaba una, quedara expuesto a la siguiente. En el extremo está la Garita del Diablo, donde, según la leyenda, los guardias de la noche simplemente desaparecían.
scripts.fr: San Cristóbal regardait dans l’autre sens qu’El Morro : il protégeait San Juan d’une attaque par la terre. Achevé à la fin du dix-huitième siècle, c’est la plus grande fortification bâtie par l’Espagne dans les Amériques, avec des remparts superposés : prendre l’un laissait l’assaillant exposé au suivant. Tout au bout se dresse la Garita del Diablo, la guérite du diable, où, selon la légende, des sentinelles de nuit disparurent sans laisser de trace.
scripts.pt: San Cristóbal olhava para o lado oposto ao de El Morro: protegia San Juan de um ataque por terra. Concluído no fim do século dezoito, é a maior fortificação que a Espanha construiu nas Américas, com muralhas em camadas, para que quem tomasse uma ficasse exposto à seguinte. Na ponta fica a Garita del Diablo, a guarita do diabo, onde, diz a lenda, sentinelas do turno da noite simplesmente sumiam.
scripts.de: San Cristóbal blickte in die andere Richtung als El Morro: Es schützte San Juan vor einem Angriff über Land. Fertiggestellt im späten achtzehnten Jahrhundert, ist es die größte Festung, die Spanien in Amerika gebaut hat, mit Mauer hinter Mauer, damit ein Angreifer nach jeder eroberten Mauer der nächsten ausgesetzt war. Ganz am Ende steht die Garita del Diablo, das Wachhäuschen des Teufels, in dem der Legende nach Wachen in der Nacht spurlos verschwanden.
scripts.it: San Cristóbal guardava dalla parte opposta rispetto a El Morro: proteggeva San Juan da un attacco via terra. Completato alla fine del Settecento, è la più grande fortificazione costruita dalla Spagna nelle Americhe, con mura su mura, così che chi ne conquistava una restava esposto alla successiva. All’estremità c’è la Garita del Diablo, la garitta del diavolo, dove secondo la leggenda le sentinelle di notte sparivano nel nulla.

closed_source.text: National Park Service, San Juan National Historic Site

access.note: Several levels joined by ramps and stairs. You can see a lot from the main level and skip the climb to the Garita del Diablo.

name: Paseo de la Princesa
description: A flat, tree-lined promenade under the city walls, from the Raíces fountain by the bay to the walk toward the old San Juan Gate.
tips: Artisans and food stalls set up here, mostly on weekends and holidays.
Lovely at sunset, when it cools down.

audio.script: The Paseo de la Princesa is a nineteenth century promenade below the city walls, named after a Spanish princess. The long pink building was once a prison; today it houses the island’s tourism offices. At the end, the Raíces fountain, Roots, celebrates the three peoples who made Puerto Rico: the Taíno who lived here first, the Spanish who arrived in 1508, and the Africans who were brought here. Keep walking along the walls toward the old San Juan Gate.

scripts.es: El Paseo de la Princesa es un paseo del siglo diecinueve al pie de las murallas, nombrado en honor a una princesa española. El largo edificio rosado fue una cárcel; hoy alberga oficinas de turismo de la isla. Al final, la fuente Raíces celebra los tres pueblos que formaron Puerto Rico: los taínos, que vivían aquí primero, los españoles, que llegaron en 1508, y los africanos que fueron traídos a la isla. Sigue caminando junto a las murallas hacia la antigua Puerta de San Juan.
scripts.fr: Le Paseo de la Princesa est une promenade du dix-neuvième siècle au pied des remparts, baptisée en l’honneur d’une princesse espagnole. Le long bâtiment rose fut une prison ; il abrite aujourd’hui des bureaux du tourisme de l’île. Au bout, la fontaine Raíces, les Racines, célèbre les trois peuples qui ont fait Porto Rico : les Taïnos, premiers habitants, les Espagnols, arrivés en 1508, et les Africains amenés sur l’île. Continuez le long des remparts vers l’ancienne porte de San Juan.
scripts.pt: O Paseo de la Princesa é um passeio do século dezenove ao pé das muralhas, batizado em homenagem a uma princesa espanhola. O longo prédio cor-de-rosa já foi uma prisão; hoje abriga escritórios de turismo da ilha. No fim, a fonte Raíces celebra os três povos que formaram Porto Rico: os taínos, que viviam aqui primeiro, os espanhóis, que chegaram em 1508, e os africanos que foram trazidos para a ilha. Siga caminhando junto às muralhas até a antiga Porta de San Juan.
scripts.de: Der Paseo de la Princesa ist eine Promenade aus dem neunzehnten Jahrhundert unterhalb der Stadtmauern, benannt nach einer spanischen Prinzessin. Das lange rosa Gebäude war einst ein Gefängnis; heute sitzen dort Tourismusbüros der Insel. Am Ende feiert der Brunnen Raíces, Wurzeln, die drei Völker, die Puerto Rico geprägt haben: die Taíno, die zuerst hier lebten, die Spanier, die 1508 kamen, und die Afrikaner, die auf die Insel gebracht wurden. Gehen Sie an der Mauer entlang weiter zum alten Tor von San Juan.
scripts.it: Il Paseo de la Princesa è una passeggiata ottocentesca ai piedi delle mura, dedicata a una principessa spagnola. Il lungo edificio rosa era un carcere; oggi ospita uffici del turismo dell’isola. In fondo, la fontana Raíces, Radici, celebra i tre popoli che hanno fatto Porto Rico: i Taíno, che vivevano qui per primi, gli spagnoli, arrivati nel 1508, e gli africani portati sull’isola. Continuate lungo le mura verso l’antica Porta di San Juan.

access.note: Flat and paved, with benches and shade trees. The easiest walk in Old San Juan.

name: Catedral de San Juan Bautista
area: Calle del Cristo, Old San Juan
description: One of the oldest cathedrals in the Americas, begun in the 1520s and largely rebuilt in the 1800s. Juan Ponce de León’s tomb is inside.
tips: A working church: dress modestly, and stay quiet during Mass.
Visiting times shift around services, especially at Christmas; check the door.

audio.script: San Juan’s cathedral was begun in the fifteen twenties, which makes it one of the oldest in the Americas, though storms and time meant much of what you see was rebuilt in the eighteen hundreds. Inside lies Juan Ponce de León, the first Spanish governor of Puerto Rico. Outside, notice the street itself: the bluish stones are adoquines, cast from furnace slag. The story goes that they crossed the Atlantic as ballast in Spanish ships.

scripts.es: La catedral de San Juan se comenzó en la década de 1520, lo que la convierte en una de las más antiguas de las Américas, aunque las tormentas y el tiempo hicieron que gran parte de lo que ves se reconstruyera en el siglo diecinueve. Dentro descansa Juan Ponce de León, el primer gobernador español de Puerto Rico. Afuera, fíjate en la calle: las piedras azuladas son adoquines hechos de escoria de fundición. Se cuenta que cruzaron el Atlántico como lastre en barcos españoles.
scripts.fr: La cathédrale de San Juan a été commencée dans les années 1520, ce qui en fait l’une des plus anciennes des Amériques, même si les tempêtes et le temps ont imposé de reconstruire une grande partie de ce que vous voyez au dix-neuvième siècle. À l’intérieur repose Juan Ponce de León, premier gouverneur espagnol de Porto Rico. Dehors, regardez la rue : les pavés bleutés sont des adoquines, coulés à partir de scories de fonderie. On raconte qu’ils ont traversé l’Atlantique comme lest dans les navires espagnols.
scripts.pt: A catedral de San Juan foi iniciada nos anos 1520, o que a torna uma das mais antigas das Américas, embora tempestades e o tempo tenham feito com que boa parte do que você vê fosse reconstruída no século dezenove. Lá dentro está o túmulo de Juan Ponce de León, o primeiro governador espanhol de Porto Rico. Lá fora, repare na rua: as pedras azuladas são adoquines, feitos de escória de fundição. Dizem que atravessaram o Atlântico como lastro em navios espanhóis.
scripts.de: Mit dem Bau der Kathedrale von San Juan wurde in den 1520er-Jahren begonnen, damit ist sie eine der ältesten in Amerika, auch wenn Stürme und die Zeit dazu führten, dass vieles von dem, was Sie sehen, im neunzehnten Jahrhundert neu gebaut wurde. Drinnen ruht Juan Ponce de León, der erste spanische Gouverneur Puerto Ricos. Draußen lohnt ein Blick auf die Straße: Die bläulichen Steine sind Adoquines, gegossen aus Hochofenschlacke. Es heißt, sie seien als Ballast in spanischen Schiffen über den Atlantik gekommen.
scripts.it: La cattedrale di San Juan fu iniziata negli anni Venti del Cinquecento, il che la rende una delle più antiche delle Americhe, anche se tempeste e tempo hanno fatto ricostruire gran parte di ciò che vedete nell’Ottocento. All’interno riposa Juan Ponce de León, il primo governatore spagnolo di Porto Rico. Fuori, guardate la strada: le pietre azzurrine sono adoquines, fusi dalle scorie di fonderia. Si racconta che attraversarono l’Atlantico come zavorra sulle navi spagnole.

access.note: The church itself is easy, but Calle del Cristo slopes and is paved with blue cobblestones. Come by car to the door if walking is hard.

name: Capilla del Cristo and Parque de las Palomas
description: A tiny 18th-century chapel at the end of Calle del Cristo and, beside it, a little park full of pigeons with a view over the bay. A good place to sit.
tips: The chapel opens only at limited times; you can see in through its gates.
Kids love feeding the pigeons; birdseed is often sold nearby.

access.note: Downhill to get there and uphill back. Benches in the park. A taxi to the bottom of Calle del Cristo saves the climb.

name: Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico
description: Puerto Rican art from the 1600s to today, in a 1920s hospital building, with a sculpture garden. Cool, calm and air-conditioned.
tips: Open Wednesday, Friday and Saturday 10:00 to 17:00, Thursday 10:00 to 20:00 (free from 17:00), Sunday 11:00 to 17:00.
Closed Mondays, Tuesdays and holidays.
The sculpture garden opens daily except holidays.

closed_source.text: Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico, mapr.org

access.note: Indoors, cool and on level floors: a good break from the heat.

name: Calle Cerra murals
description: A street of huge, ever-changing murals from the Santurce es Ley festival, with bars and small galleries between them. Bright, photogenic and very local.
tips: Go in daylight for photos; in the evening the area gets lively.
At night, take a ride back rather than walking far.

access.note: A flat street, but there’s little shade at midday.

name: La Placita de Santurce
description: A market square that sells fruit and vegetables by day and turns into a big street party at night, especially Thursday to Saturday, with salsa, bars and restaurants all around.
tips: For seats, book a table at one of the restaurants around the square.
It’s loud and crowded on weekend nights; go earlier with kids.

access.note: Mostly standing room on busy nights. The restaurants around the square have tables.

food.note: Lots of choice around the square: grilled fish and mofongo, but also pizza and chicken.

name: Balneario El Escambrón
description: A calm, reef-protected beach between Old San Juan and Condado, with a lifeguard, restrooms and outdoor showers. The city’s best swim for non-swimmers.
tips: A lifeguard is on duty from about 8:30 or 9:30 to 17:30. Check before you swim.
The west corner is the shallowest and clearest.
Free on foot; parking is about $6 a car.
Check the day’s flag on SwimSafePR (swimsafepr.com) before going in.

access.note: A ramp leads onto the sand; ask at the ticket booth for help. Restrooms on the west side.

ride: Uber and taxis drop off at the parking lot, 5 to 10 minutes from Old San Juan or Condado.

name: Balneario de Carolina
description: Isla Verde’s public beach: wide sand, lifeguards and paramedics, a small water park for kids and gazebos to rent. Awarded the Blue Flag for clean water.
tips: From August 16 to May 14: open Tuesday to Sunday, 8:00 to 17:00; closed Mondays unless it’s a holiday.
Rent a gazebo for the day for shade and seats.
It closes when the surf is dangerous, as it did in April 2026.
Check the day’s flag on SwimSafePR (swimsafepr.com) before going in.
closed_note: Closed Mondays (Aug 16 to May 14), unless a holiday

closed_source.text: Discover Puerto Rico, Balneario de Carolina

access.note: Gazebos give the whole family shade and seats. Winter waves can be strong; swim near the lifeguards.

name: Playa de Ocean Park
description: A long, local favorite in front of the Ocean Park neighborhood: wide sand, kitesurfers and a relaxed crowd.
tips: Lovely to sit at. It isn’t a guarded beach, and currents can be strong in winter.
Non-swimmers: stay in the shallows, or swim at El Escambrón.
Check the day’s flag on SwimSafePR (swimsafepr.com) before going in.

access.note: Flat sand and easy to reach, but bring your own shade.

name: Piñones
area: Loíza, 15 minutes east of Isla Verde
description: A coastal strip of beach shacks (kioskos) under the palms, famous for fritters like alcapurrias and bacalaítos, with a seaside boardwalk and bike path.
tips: Busiest on weekend afternoons.
Carry cash.

access.note: Counters and a few plastic chairs. Flat and easy, but hot at midday.

food.note: Most fritters are crab, fish or meat, all from the same fryers. Not ideal with a seafood allergy; ask what’s in each one.

ride: Uber reaches Piñones from San Juan. Coming back at night, drivers can be scarce: check the app before you settle in, or arrange a pickup.

name: Guided El Yunque tour from San Juan
area: El Yunque, pickup in San Juan
lead_time: Holiday week: book 2 to 3 weeks ahead. Pick a small group with hotel pickup.
description: The easy way into the rainforest: a guide, the drive both ways, and the best short walks and viewpoints. Choose an easy or family level.
tips: Ask: how easy is the walk, is there a swim stop, and where is the pickup?
El Yunque is closed on December 25.
search_q: El Yunque rainforest tour from San Juan with pickup

access.note: Tours grade their walks. Pick an easy one for older travelers.

ride: The tour’s van takes you in and out. Ride apps can’t pick up inside the forest.

name: Laguna Grande bio bay
lead_time: Book ahead: tours run after dark and sell out on holiday nights.
description: Paddle through a mangrove channel into a lagoon that glows blue-green when you move the water. The closest bio bay to San Juan, about an hour away.
tips: The full moon is December 24. After it, the moon rises later each night, so book the earliest tour for the darkest water.
No swimming, and no lotion, sunscreen or repellent in the water.
Tours here are by kayak, in pairs, through a narrow channel. For a seated boat, see La Parguera bio bay by boat.
Operators listed by Discover Puerto Rico: Kayaking Puerto Rico, (787) 245-4545, and Pure Adventure.
search_q: Laguna Grande bioluminescent bay kayak Fajardo

access.note: About an hour of paddling at night. Not for anyone unsteady in a kayak.

ride: Many tours offer pickup in San Juan. Otherwise, book a driver who waits: rides back from Fajardo late at night are hard to find.

name: La Parguera bio bay by boat

price.text: $45 to $95 a person for standard tours

lead_time: Book ahead for holiday nights. Choose a tour with round-trip transport from San Juan, or a driver who waits.
description: The seated option: a boat from La Parguera village out to a glowing bay on the southwest coast. No paddling, and swimming is often allowed. Good for families and bigger groups.
tips: About 2 to 2.5 hours’ drive each way from San Juan; boat tours last 1 to 2 hours. Expect to be back late.
The glow is softer here than at the other bays and varies by night. Go on the darkest night you can: the moon rises later each night after the December 24 full moon, so book the earliest tour.
Swimming is allowed on most nights but not guaranteed; confirm with the operator.
Operator listed by Puerto Rico travel guide topuertorico.org: Eco Action Tours, (787) 791-7509.
search_q: La Parguera bioluminescent bay boat tour from San Juan
duration: A long evening: about 7 to 8 hours door to door

access.note: You sit on the boat the whole time. Boarding can mean a step down from a dock; ask the operator about help.

ride: Rides back from La Parguera late at night are very hard to find. Book a tour with transport from San Juan, or a driver who waits.

name: Old San Juan food tour
lead_time: Tell the operator your food notes when you book.
description: Tastings of mofongo, fritters and local coffee, with stories of the city. A good first evening.

access.note: Plenty of walking on Old San Juan’s hills.

food.note: Most tours can swap dishes for no pork or pescatarian if told ahead. Check carefully with a seafood allergy.

name: El Yunque
area: Río Grande, about an hour east
description: The only tropical rainforest in the US National Forest system: waterfalls, misty peaks, the Yokahú Tower and the coquí frog’s evening song.
tips: The main road (PR-191) closes when parking is full or flash floods are possible. Start early.
Entry to the PR-191 recreation area is free, and no reservation is needed right now.
El Portal visitor center: $8 for 16 and up, daily 8:00 to 16:00; closed December 25, January 1 and January 6. It has the Puerto Rican parrot exhibit.
La Mina trail and falls are closed for construction.
The recreation area closes at 17:00; start back by 16:45.

audio.script: El Yunque is the only tropical rainforest in the United States National Forest system. Its name may come from the Taíno word yuké, white lands, for the clouds that wrap its peaks; in Spanish it sounds like the word for anvil. Listen in the evening for the coquí, a tiny frog no bigger than a thumbnail whose two-note call is the sound of Puerto Rico. And watch the sky for a flash of green: the Puerto Rican parrot, once down to a handful of birds, is slowly coming back here.

scripts.es: El Yunque es el único bosque tropical lluvioso del sistema de Bosques Nacionales de Estados Unidos. Su nombre podría venir de la palabra taína yuké, tierras blancas, por las nubes que envuelven sus picos; en español suena como el yunque del herrero. Al atardecer escucha al coquí, una ranita no más grande que una uña cuyo canto de dos notas es el sonido de Puerto Rico. Y mira al cielo por si ves un destello verde: la cotorra puertorriqueña, que llegó a quedar en apenas unos pocos ejemplares, se está recuperando poco a poco aquí.
scripts.fr: El Yunque est la seule forêt tropicale humide du réseau des forêts nationales des États-Unis. Son nom viendrait peut-être du mot taïno yuké, terres blanches, pour les nuages qui enveloppent ses sommets ; en espagnol, il sonne comme le mot enclume. Le soir, écoutez le coquí, une minuscule grenouille pas plus grande qu’un ongle, dont le chant de deux notes est le son de Porto Rico. Et guettez un éclair vert dans le ciel : l’amazone de Porto Rico, qui ne comptait plus que quelques oiseaux, revient peu à peu ici.
scripts.pt: El Yunque é a única floresta tropical úmida do sistema de Florestas Nacionais dos Estados Unidos. O nome talvez venha da palavra taína yuké, terras brancas, pelas nuvens que envolvem seus picos; em espanhol soa como a palavra bigorna. Ao entardecer, ouça o coquí, um sapinho do tamanho de uma unha cujo canto de duas notas é o som de Porto Rico. E fique de olho num lampejo verde no céu: o papagaio-de-porto-rico, que chegou a ter só alguns indivíduos, está voltando aos poucos aqui.
scripts.de: El Yunque ist der einzige tropische Regenwald im System der Nationalforste der Vereinigten Staaten. Der Name kommt vielleicht vom Taíno-Wort yuké, weiße Länder, für die Wolken um die Gipfel; auf Spanisch klingt er wie das Wort für Amboss. Hören Sie am Abend auf den Coquí, einen winzigen Frosch, nicht größer als ein Daumennagel, dessen Ruf aus zwei Tönen der Klang Puerto Ricos ist. Und achten Sie auf einen grünen Blitz am Himmel: Der Puerto-Rico-Amazonenpapagei, einst auf eine Handvoll Vögel geschrumpft, kehrt hier langsam zurück.
scripts.it: El Yunque è l’unica foresta pluviale tropicale del sistema delle Foreste Nazionali degli Stati Uniti. Il nome potrebbe venire dalla parola taína yuké, terre bianche, per le nuvole che avvolgono le sue cime; in spagnolo suona come la parola incudine. La sera ascoltate il coquí, una minuscola rana non più grande di un’unghia, il cui verso di due note è il suono di Porto Rico. E guardate il cielo per un lampo verde: l’amazzone di Porto Rico, ridotta un tempo a pochi esemplari, sta lentamente tornando qui.

how: A tour with pickup, or a driver for the day. Ride apps can’t operate in the forest, and no taxis wait there
closed_note: Closed Dec 25 (visitor center also Jan 1 and Jan 6)

closed_source.text: US Forest Service, El Yunque FAQs (updated Apr 2, 2025)

access.note: El Portal’s accessible trail and roadside viewpoints are easy. Forest trails are wet, rooty and steep in places.

ride: Ride apps and taxis can’t pick up inside El Yunque. Book a tour with round-trip pickup, or a driver who stays with you.

name: Luquillo and the kioskos
description: A palm-lined bay with often calmer water than San Juan’s beaches, and more than 60 food kiosks along the road behind it.
tips: The kioskos are busiest on weekends; bars stay open late Friday and Saturday.
Check the day’s flag on SwimSafePR (swimsafepr.com) before going in.
how: Combine with El Yunque on a tour, or with a driver for the day

access.note: Flat and easy, with plenty of places to sit at the kiosks.

food.note: Beyond fritters: pizza, chicken and grilled fish. With a seafood allergy, ask about the fryers.

ride: Ride apps are unreliable for the trip back from Luquillo. Go with a tour or a driver who waits.
